components.text: Naturalism allegedly lacks an objective basis for ranking evolved human values over competing biological dispositions.
Natural facts allegedly cannot make conduct or preferences objectively wrong without an authoritative imperative.
Explain why evolved or culturally endorsed preferences can nevertheless be objectively mistaken rather than merely different.
Explain how objective error about conduct yields genuinely binding obligation rather than only an evaluative comparison.
Natural minds and welfare-governing facts allegedly make moral truth amenable to scientific investigation.
Values may be objectively mistaken when they reliably frustrate well-being.
Explain why the worst-misery evaluative anchor fails to provide an objective natural standard.
Answer the claim that natural facts governing minds and well-being are open to scientific investigation.
The welfare continuum allegedly supplies an objective moral standard connecting better states with moral goodness.
Natural facts governing welfare allegedly suffice for scientific understanding of moral truth.
Show that the continuum of conscious well-being is identical with, or sufficient to ground, the full domain of moral goodness.
Show that scientifically investigable facts about flourishing exhaust the facts relevant to moral value.
God's necessarily good nature allegedly supplies a nonarbitrary ontological standard of moral value.
A well-being axiom allegedly constitutes an illicit definitional maneuver rather than a substantive moral foundation.
Explain why identifying God's nature as intrinsically good provides a nonarbitrary standard rather than a stipulative definition.
Show that theism supplies an independently warranted objective foundation unavailable to naturalism.
Apply the same objection to Harris's own axiomatic starting point without assuming the desired moral conclusion.
Defining God as intrinsically good allegedly fails to supply an independent, nonarbitrary ground of goodness.
Explain why essential divine goodness follows from the concept of God rather than from arbitrary stipulation.
Address whether an evil god or several evil gods remain genuine conceptual alternatives.
God's essential goodness allegedly follows from maximal greatness and worship-worthiness rather than arbitrary definition.
Divine nature and commands allegedly provide an objective moral foundation.
Show that the conceptual argument for essential divine goodness fails or is equally available to an incompatible deity.
Distinguish the truth of a supernatural ontological foundation from reliable epistemic access through a particular revelation.
Address the explicit distinction between moral ontology and epistemic disagreement.
A maximally great, worship-worthy God's essential goodness allegedly grounds objective values.
Moral ontology should be separated from language, knowledge, and disputed access.
Answer the distinction between an objective moral foundation and fallible epistemic access to that foundation.
Explain why honest inquiry defeats the conceptual claim that a maximally great God is essentially good.
Explain how honest inquiry resolves the alleged modal divergence between well-being and moral goodness.
Objective obligation allegedly requires competent authoritative imperatives rather than natural facts about flourishing.
Divine commands consistent with a good nature allegedly constitute moral duties.
Explain why competent authority is insufficient to constitute moral duty when an authorized act still inflicts recognizable harm.
Address the qualification that divine commands are necessarily constrained by a holy and loving nature.
Show why an essentially good authority could nevertheless issue a genuinely harmful command.
Commands grounded in God's holy and loving nature allegedly constitute objective duties without arbitrariness.
A maximally great and worship-worthy God allegedly cannot issue an evil command.
Explain whether a purported divine command can be morally condemned independently of its asserted authoritative source.
Address the claim that the genuine greatest conceivable God is essentially good and therefore cannot issue an evil command.
Explain what natural or independent foundation gives the condemning judgment objective authority.
Competing inherited revelations allegedly undermine the objective supernatural foundation because they produce incompatible moral claims.
Shared honest inquiry allegedly should replace sectarian revelation as the route to moral truth.
Explain why disagreement and unreliable sectarian access do not by themselves defeat the existence or supernatural ground of objective moral facts.
Address whether shared honest inquiry is epistemically preferable to competing revelation claims.
Explain how applied moral judgment relates to the asserted divine ontological foundation.
